about.body:
Cybersecurity MSc graduate
awarded the NCR Atleos Prize for Best Student of the Programme.

Focused on Digital Forensics, Security Engineering and Secure Software Development.

Bridging offensive security and defensive engineering, from penetration testing to secure system architecture.

Security and privacy are part of the process from the very beginning.
about.remark: Currently available for freelance engagements and open to employment opportunities.

keys.title: Focus Areas
keys.services: Skills include, but are not limited to:

project-1.title: Mobile & Computer Forensics Case Studies (Academic Lab)
project-1.summary: Conducted two structured digital forensic investigations involving 56 mobile and cloud extraction files across multiple devices and online accounts, as well as a 5 GB disk image. Performed evidence triage, artifact analysis, event reconstruction and cross-source correlation to produce expert witness-style forensic reports containing evidence inventories, timeline visualisations and evidence-supported investigative findings.
general: Conducted forensic examinations across 56 extraction files derived from mobile devices, SIM cards, tablets and cloud-based accounts, including social media, email and cloud storage data.
Performed artifact analysis across messaging applications, documents, images, browser activity, device configurations, system artifacts and user-generated content.
Analysed a 5 GB disk image through operating system auditing, deleted partition recovery, keyword searching, malware scanning and registry examination.
Correlated evidence from mobile, cloud and endpoint sources to reconstruct user activities, establish event sequences and resolve timestamp discrepancies across multiple time zones.
Produced expert witness-style forensic reports including evidence inventories, examination methodology, visualised timelines, event reconstruction and evidence-supported hypotheses.
specific: Analysed evidence from 17 physical devices and 12 cloud/social media accounts (overall 56+ forensic extraction files), consolidating findings into a unified investigative assessment.
Reconstructed user activity and event timelines through correlation of messaging, browser, cloud, registry and file system artifacts across multiple evidence sources.

Delivered two comprehensive forensic reports containing evidence inventories, timeline visualisations, examination procedures and evidence-supported conclusions suitable for formal investigative review.
Identified and prioritised high-value forensic artifacts from diverse evidence sources, enabling efficient investigation and response decision-making.
Supported incident scoping and post-incident analysis through event reconstruction, deleted data recovery, malware assessment and user activity analysis.
Provided actionable findings and evidence-based hypotheses that inform containment, remediation planning and follow-up investigative activities.

project-2.title: Digital Forensics Case Management Framework & Tool Prototype (Master Thesis)
project-2.summary: Researched digital forensics case management through an analysis of 20 academic papers and 5 additional industry sources, deriving an 8-module requirements framework for forensic case management systems. Based on a comparative assessment of 6 existing solutions, designed and prototyped a security-by-design digital forensics case management platform addressing 20 forensic and security properties, with a focus on evidence integrity, chain of custody, auditability and investigator workflows.
project-2.remark: Currently being written up as a paper.
general: Conducted a structured literature review of 20 academic publications and 5 industry sources to identify digital forensics case management requirements and best practices.
Developed an 8-module requirements framework covering forensic workflows, evidence management, chain of custody, security & risk controls and case lifecycle tracking.
Evaluated 6 forensic case management solutions against the framework and performed a gap analysis to identify usability, security and capability deficiencies.
Designed a microservices-based architecture consisting of 16 services with defined trust boundaries, RBAC, audit logging, integrity validation and security-by-design principles.
Developed a proof-of-concept implementation using FastAPI, React, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker Compose and Keycloak to validate architecture and usability.
specific: Established an 8-module forensic case management framework derived from 25 research and industry sources, translating forensic best practices into actionable system requirements.
Identified capability, workflow and security gaps across 6 existing forensic case management solutions and incorporated findings into the target architecture.
Designed a system addressing 20 forensic and security properties, including evidence integrity, chain of custody, auditability, access control and investigation traceability.

Designed a 16-microservice architecture and implemented a proof-of-concept consisting of 5 partially implemented services, including an API Gateway, Keycloak integration and supporting backend services with Redis integration.
Developed a React/MUI frontend comprising 12 pages and 25 reusable components, supported by 2 REST APIs and WebSocket integration.
Implemented a PostgreSQL data layer with 5 database models, SQLAlchemy ORM mappings and Pydantic schemas, fully containerised using Docker Compose.

project-3.title: Forensic Artifact Processing Automation Tool (Open Source)
project-3.summary: Designed and developed a cross-platform forensic artifact processing and reporting tool in Python that partially automates the analysis of recovered files. The Docker-based solution parses Foremost file carving outputs, extracts and normalises metadata using ExifTool, detects duplicate files, stores results in PostgreSQL and generates structured JSON reports, reducing manual triage effort and improving investigation efficiency.
project-3.remark: Open-source beta release available on GitHub.
general: Designed and developed a platform-independent Python CLI application for automated forensic artifact processing and reporting.
Implemented parsing functionality for Foremost file-carving outputs to transform recovered files into structured data.
Integrated ExifTool to extract and normalise 30+ metadata fields from disk images and individual recovered files.
Developed duplicate detection logic to identify redundant artifacts and improve evidence review efficiency.
Built a Docker-based solution with PostgreSQL storage, JSON report generation, input validation, error handling and cross-platform startup scripts using Bash and PowerShell.
specific: Applied forensic file processing workflows including file carving analysis, metadata extraction and automated triage using a test dataset of nearly 10,000 files.
Developed practical understanding of how metadata normalisation and duplicate detection support evidence correlation, filtering and efficient forensic investigation workflows.
Built an automated DFIR processing pipeline that transforms raw forensic outputs into structured investigation data and reports, reducing repetitive manual analysis steps.
Applied the software development lifecycle by performing requirements analysis, solution design, implementation, testing and deployment for a forensic automation tool.
Designed and implemented a 7-stage processing pipeline covering ingestion, parsing, metadata extraction, duplicate detection, database storage, report generation and cleanup.
Developed a maintainable cross-platform application architecture using Python, Docker and PostgreSQL with 3 database models and automated execution through Bash and PowerShell startup scripts.

project-4.title: Manual Open-Source Web Application Security Assessment (Real-World)
project-4.summary: Conducted a full manual security assessment of a zero-knowledge open-source web application in a local VM environment. Performed a manual security assessment of a zero-knowledge open-source web application in a local VM environment. Identified security flaws, business logic issues and social engineering risks through code review, traffic analysis and browser-based testing.
general: Set up and tested a zero-knowledge open-source web application in a local VM environment
Performed basic code review and analysed application behaviour through browser/UI testing
Used Burp Suite for network traffic analysis, request manipulation and attack validation
Tested for XSS, CSRF, business logic flaws, validation weaknesses and client-side bypasses
Identified security bugs and social engineering/phishing possibilities, then documented and disclosed findings responsibly
specific: Improved manual web application testing skills beyond automated vulnerability scanning
Gained hands-on experience with Burp Suite, browser analysis, request manipulation and exploit validation
Learned how business logic flaws and social engineering opportunities can create realistic attack paths
Developed a stronger understanding of secure validation, trust boundaries and client–server security design
Learned how weak input validation and client-side controls can lead to exploitable security gaps
Improved vulnerability classification, reporting and communication with developers during responsible disclosure processes

project-5.title: Windows Domain Security Assessment (Academic Lab)
project-5.summary: Performed a hands-on penetration test against a Windows Active Directory lab environment simulating common enterprise weaknesses. Identified and exploited misconfigurations leading to credential compromise, privilege escalation and system-level access.
general: Performed network and service enumeration with Nmap across SMB, DNS, SMTP, FTP, RDP and SSH
Used Nessus and manual validation to identify vulnerabilities and exposed services
Analysed Active Directory users, authentication mechanisms, password policies and service configurations
Exploited misconfigurations for credential harvesting, password cracking, privilege escalation and admin account compromise
Gained system-level access on a target server and documented attack paths and remediation recommendations
specific: Improved practical Active Directory pentesting skills from enumeration to full system compromise
Gained hands-on experience with Nmap, Nessus, credential attacks and privilege escalation techniques
Learned how multiple small weaknesses can be chained into realistic enterprise attack paths
Developed a stronger understanding of common Windows AD misconfigurations and hardening practices
Learned how weak authentication, permissions and exposed services increase enterprise attack surface
Improved technical reporting, root cause analysis and remediation recommendation skills

project-6.title: OWASP-based Web Application Pentest (Academic Lab)
project-6.summary: Performed a methodology-driven web application penetration test based on the OWASP Testing Guide, combining automated scanning with manual validation and exploitation. Identified and demonstrated vulnerabilities including SQL injection, XSS, broken authentication, session hijacking and business logic flaws in a realistic attack scenario.
general: Conducted reconnaissance and attack surface mapping against the target web application
Tested authentication, authorisation, session management, input validation and business logic
Used OWASP ZAP, Wapiti, and Nessus to identify vulnerabilities and manually validate findings

Exploited SQL injection for database access using manual techniques and sqlmap, leveraged XSS with BeEF hook for client-side control, used Weevely for post-exploitation activities and demonstrated admin session replay attacks
Documented confirmed findings, exploitation evidence, attack paths and mitigation recommendations in a structured report
specific: Improved practical web application pentesting skills using the OWASP Testing Guide as a structured methodology
Gained hands-on experience exploiting SQLi, XSS, broken authentication, session hijacking and business logic vulnerabilities
Learned how to validate automated scan results manually and chain vulnerabilities into realistic attack scenarios

project-7.title: Linux Home Server
project-7.summary: Deployed and maintained a self-hosted Raspberry Pi Linux server for 3+ years, providing remote file access and backup services through Nextcloud, SMB and OpenVPN. Secured and administered the environment entirely through CLI-based Linux system administration, hardening and monitoring practices.
general: Deployed and configured Nextcloud, SMB and OpenVPN services on a Raspberry Pi-based Linux server.
Applied system hardening measures, such as iptables and fail2ban configurations, SSH security best practices and user management and least privilege access control.
Performed 30+ monthly maintenance cycles including updates and upgrades, troubleshooting, log review and basic network traffic review.
Managed the environment through CLI/Bash administration, including shell scripts for automatic updates and service monitoring.
Created comprehensive technical documentation of setup and configuration steps for reproducibility and faster issue resolution.
specific: Gained hands-on experience hardening Linux systems across different system areas and reducing attack surface in a self-hosted environment.
Learned secure remote-access practices and VPN configuration with OpenVPN.
Improved operational security skills through continuous monitoring, troubleshooting and log analysis.
Strengthened Linux administration and command-line skills through 3+ years of hands-on system management.
Gained experience deploying and maintaining infrastructure services for file sharing, backups and remote access.
Developed structured troubleshooting and technical documentation practices for reliable system operation and reproducible setups.

project-8.title: Cryptanalysis of DiCal-IDEA implementation (Bachelor Thesis)
project-8.summary: Conducted a structured analysis of the DiCal-IDEA encryption used in the POCSAG protocol for BOS paging systems. Analysed 236 ciphertext samples, protocol metadata and public resources to identify likely message structures, encryption methods and IV handling through ciphertext-only and hypothesis-driven analysis, followed by threat modelling of potential weaknesses and attack vectors.
general: Researched existing cryptanalysis and technical documentation related to the IDEA cipher and DiCal-IDEA implementations
Analysed encrypted POCSAG message datasets and correlated ciphertext patterns with protocol metadata and timestamps
Developed and tested multiple hypotheses regarding message structure, cipher mode operation, IV usage and nonce construction
Applied exclusion-based analytical methods to identify technically plausible encryption implementations
Produced a threat modelling assessment of the identified and hypothesised cryptographic design choices
specific: Analysed proprietary cryptographic implementations with limited technical information
Identified potential attack vectors and weaknesses through threat modelling and protocol analysis
Improved hypothesis-driven security analysis and technical validation methodologies
Conducted structured investigations on encrypted communication datasets
Performed metadata correlation, protocol artifact analysis and timeline-based investigation methods
Documented technical findings in clear, structured and evidence-based analytical reports

experience-1.title: Cybersecurity Student Assistant (Part-Time)
experience-1.summary: Designed and secured a penetration testing training environment featuring realistic attack scenarios, hands-on exercises and controlled responsible disclosure workflows. Developed supporting documentation, operational procedures and security controls to enable a structured and secure training platform.
general: Designed a penetration testing lab architecture with realistic attack scenarios and offensive security exercises.
Developed structured training documentation and methodology-based exercise materials.
Defined security controls including firewall (iptables) rules, user management, access control restrictions and SSH security best practices for the training environment.
Designed a responsible disclosure process and documented disclosure policies for controlled security testing activities.
Created comprehensive technical documentation of the server setup to enable ongoing maintenance and expansion.
specific: Developed a structured framework for realistic penetration testing exercises and attack simulations.
Designed training scenarios aligned with common penetration testing methodologies and offensive security workflows.
Expanded understanding of attack path design, adversary simulation and practical training environment development.
Defined security architecture concepts including access control, system boundaries and permission management.
Applied security engineering principles to balance usability and risk reduction.
Strengthened knowledge of trust boundaries, operational security controls and secure environment design.

experience-2.title: Data Privacy & Security Intern (Full-time)
experience-2.summary: Supported GDPR compliance and web application security initiatives within a university environment by analysing data processing activities, assessing PII-related risks, conducting scoped vulnerability assessments and collaborating with administrators to strengthen data protection controls and security posture.
general: Conducted comprehensive research on GDPR requirements, European data privacy regulations and relevant legal case law to support compliance assessments.
Analysed institutional data flows and mapped personal data processing activities to identify compliance obligations and privacy risks.
Created and maintained Records of Processing Activities (RoPA) documentation and supported GDPR governance processes.
Assessed university web applications to identify PII collection, processing and storage points, evaluating associated privacy and security risks.
Performed scoped web application vulnerability assessments, triaged findings based on risk and impact, and collaborated with system administrators to support remediation efforts.
specific: Assessed personal data processing activities across 11 functional areas of a university web application, identifying PII processing points and associated privacy risks.
Analysed institutional data flows and supported GDPR compliance efforts through the creation of RoPA documentation and data processing assessments.
Improved visibility into personal data handling practices by mapping data processing activities and evaluating compliance of GDPR principles.
Conducted scoped security assessments across 2 university web applications, identifying vulnerabilities and security weaknesses affecting web-facing services.
Reported 5 validated security findings through a structured responsible disclosure process, enabling risk-based remediation by system administrators.
Performed vulnerability triage and impact assessment to prioritise remediation efforts and reduce exposure to identified application security risks.

experience-3.title: Software Developer - Forensic Lab Equipment (Part-time)
experience-3.summary: Independently refactored and extended a legacy C# desktop application used for forensic lab equipment log processing. Improved code structure, redesigned GUI-based data visualisation and rebuilt documentation while collaborating with hardware and sales stakeholders.
general: Independently refactored and extended a legacy C# Windows desktop application used for forensic log processing
Restructured existing code and applied design patterns to improve maintainability, readability and data handling
Redesigned the GUI-based log visualisation to make data easier to analyse and report
Rebuilt technical documentation to reflect the updated system architecture and workflows
Collaborated with hardware and sales stakeholders to ensure accurate data representation and user-friendly output while managing version control with SVN
specific: Gained hands-on experience working with and improving a legacy C# codebase independently
Strengthened understanding of refactoring, software architecture and design patterns in a real production environment
Improved communication skills by translating technical requirements into practical features and clear user-facing functionality

education-1.title: Master of Science in Ethical Hacking & Cybersecurity
education-1.prize: NCR Atleos Prize for Best Student of the Programme
education-1.summary: Completed a Master's degree covering advanced cybersecurity topics including digital forensics, penetration testing, network security, basic malware analysis and incident response, basic information security governance and data privacy law.
education-1.thesis: The master's thesis focused on designing a Digital Forensics Case Management Framework and Tool Prototype, optimising workflows, evidence handling and usability.

education-2.title: Bachelor of Science in Applied Computer Science
education-2.grades: Graduated 1.7 - Equivalent to UK Upper Second Class Honours (2:1)
education-2.summary: Completed a Bachelor's degree building a broad foundation across software development, networking, system administration, databases, with lectures on AI, mobile forensics and European data privacy law.
education-2.thesis: The bachelor's thesis involved a cryptographic analysis of a proprietary IDEA implementation.

certificate-1.title: CCNA Routing and Switching: Introduction to Networks
certificate-1.summary: Completed the Cisco CCNA Routing & Switching: Introduction to Networks course through hands-on networking labs using Cisco hardware and Packet Tracer. Configured, tested and troubleshot network environments while applying networking fundamentals including TCP/IP, subnetting, switching, routing, VLANs and WAN technologies.
general: Applied TCP/IP, OSI model, subnetting, VLANs, switching and routing concepts to design and configure network environments.
Configured Cisco routers and switches via CLI, including IP addressing, device setup and basic network administration.
Built and validated small-to-medium network topologies using Cisco hardware, Windows endpoints and Packet Tracer simulations.
Implemented routing, WAN connectivity and wireless networking scenarios while analysing hardware-level data transmission.
Diagnosed and resolved network connectivity issues through structured troubleshooting and connectivity testing.
specific: Successfully built and validated 10+ small-to-medium network topologies in lab and simulation environments.
Strengthened analytical problem-solving skills through systematic network fault identification and resolution.
Demonstrated networking proficiency by successfully deploying and resolving connectivity issues across multiple multi-subnet environments.

reference-1.body: I have known Blue since his enrolment on the MSc Ethical Hacking programme at Abertay in September 2024, when he took my Digital Forensics class. Blue quickly stood out as an exceptionally capable student, bringing intelligence, diligence and thoroughness to every task. His approach to complex problems was mature, methodical and determined, underpinned by a genuine enthusiasm for the subject. It was therefore no surprise when Blue was awarded the NCR Atleos Prize for Best Student on the Programme. Beyond his academic strengths, Blue is thoughtful, reliable, engaging and easy to work with: a real asset to any team.

reference-2.body: During his time as my student, he consistently demonstrated a strong work ethic, excellent attendance, and a genuine willingness to engage with both the course material and wider class discussions. He approached his studies with professionalism and maturity and contributed positively to the learning environment throughout. What particularly distinguished him from his peers was his attention to detail. He completed his work carefully and thoughtfully, often demonstrating a high level of precision. His commitment to producing sound work, combined with his enthusiasm for learning, made him a standout student.

reference-3.body: Blue consistently demonstrated reliability and professionalism. He was punctual, arrived prepared and ready to begin work. His self-directed approach meant he took initiative, managed tasks independently, and required minimal supervision. Blue also showed strong discipline and maintained steady progress on all assigned work. Overall, it was encouraging to see his commitment to producing quality work.

values.subtitle: This page explains if, how and by whom personal data is processed.
values.website:
This website does not collect, store or process any personal data of visitors. This website does not use cookies or any form of tracking (incl. Google Analytics).

This website may contain links to third-party services such as LinkedIn or GitHub. When visiting those external websites, personal data and technical information, such as IP addresses, browser information or request data, may be automatically processed by the respective providers.

Please refer to their respective privacy policies for more details.
